summary: Returns paginated transaction-level search rows for a filtered advanced-search population. Live probes confirmed HTTP 200 availability, transaction-grain rows, dynamic derived objects, helper ids on every row, hard sort-in-fields validation, the special no intersection short-circuit, and an agency-scoped Department of Defense screening pattern.
businessPurpose: Use this endpoint when you need to inspect the actual transactions behind a complex USAspending filter set, especially when award-level summaries would hide modifications, individual obligation events, or transaction-specific dates and descriptions.
analyticalGrain: One result row per matching transaction record from the transaction search index, not one row per award.

primaryEntities.name: Transaction row
primaryEntities.description: A single transaction matched by the advanced-search filters, with requested projected fields and helper ids for the parent award.

primaryEntities.name: Parent award reference
primaryEntities.description: Each transaction row carries generated_internal_id and internal_id for the award that owns the transaction.

primaryEntities.name: Filtered transaction population
primaryEntities.description: The underlying set of transactions selected by AdvancedFilterObject before the fields list, sort, and pagination are applied.

measures.name: Transaction Amount
measures.description: Transaction-level federal_action_obligation value on each returned row when requested. It describes the obligation recorded on that individual transaction, not a lifetime award amount.

measures.name: Loan Value
measures.description: Loan-value measure available for applicable loan-family transaction rows when requested.

measures.name: Subsidy Cost
measures.description: Loan subsidy-cost measure available for applicable loan-family transaction rows when requested.

dimensions.name: Action date
dimensions.description: Docs describe transaction search time filtering on action_date, and the Action Date field can also be projected into response rows.

dimensions.name: Award family and type
dimensions.description: award_type_codes shape the eligible population, and Award Type can be projected into response rows.

dimensions.name: Agencies
dimensions.description: The filters object supports awarding and funding agency filters, and rows can project awarding and funding agency names.

dimensions.name: Recipient and recipient geography
dimensions.description: Rows can be filtered by recipient text or location and can project Recipient Name, Recipient UEI, recipient_id, and the derived Recipient Location object. A live 2026-05-20 preview confirmed Recipient Location returns a nested object with country/state/city/county/address/congressional/zip and foreign-postal keys.

dimensions.name: Primary place of performance
dimensions.description: Filters can scope place of performance, and rows can project a derived Primary Place of Performance object.

dimensions.name: Industry and product/service classification
dimensions.description: NAICS and PSC can be used in filters and also projected as derived code+description objects.

dimensions.name: Parent-award handoff key
dimensions.description: generated_internal_id is the transaction-row identity handle for the parent award and should be preserved as row context.

suitableQuestions.name: Which transactions matched this filter set?
suitableQuestions.description: Use this endpoint when the answer needs row-level transactions rather than grouped totals or one row per award.

suitableQuestions.name: What are the largest transaction obligations in a bounded contract slice?
suitableQuestions.description: Use a bounded time_period, contract award_type_codes, and sort by Transaction Amount descending to screen the biggest transaction rows.

suitableQuestions.name: Which transactions carry useful parent-award context?
suitableQuestions.description: Use transaction search to identify interesting rows, then retain generated_internal_id as parent-award context for future promoted bundles.

suitableQuestions.name: Which transactions have a particular recipient, location, or agency context?
suitableQuestions.description: The shared filters plus projection-driven row fields let you inspect transactions by recipient, agency, place of performance, NAICS, PSC, and assistance-listing context.

suitableQuestions.name: What are the largest contract transactions for a specific awarding agency in a bounded period?
suitableQuestions.description: Use filters.agencies with a toptier or subtier object, then sort by Transaction Amount descending for a compact agency-scoped transaction screen.

notSuitableFor.name: One-row-per-award analysis
notSuitableFor.description: This endpoint can return multiple rows for the same award because the grain is transaction-level.

notSuitableFor.name: Grouped summaries or totals by category
notSuitableFor.description: This endpoint returns detail rows, not aggregated buckets by geography, time, or award type.

notSuitableFor.name: Huge bulk extraction through deep pagination
notSuitableFor.description: The validator caps limit at 100 and the source blocks requests once the page window reaches 50000 records.

notSuitableFor.name: Assuming every documented column is always present
notSuitableFor.description: Response rows are shaped by the fields request, not by a fixed default schema.

notSuitableFor.name: Using Award ID as the canonical parent-award handle
notSuitableFor.description: Award ID is display-oriented; generated_internal_id is the safer parent-award identity handle to preserve for any future promoted parent-award bundle.

joins.description: Treat generated_internal_id as the transaction-surface parent-award identity handle. This clean-slate MCP does not currently promote a downstream award-detail or funding bundle.

workflows.name: Screen high-value transaction rows
workflows.description: Use a bounded transaction search to find noteworthy obligation rows, while preserving generated_internal_id as parent-award context for future promoted bundles.

steps.action: Start with a bounded time_period and explicit award_type_codes so the transaction population is analytically scoped before paging.
Request only the fields needed for the first screen, including Transaction Amount and any context columns such as Award ID, Recipient Name, Action Date, and Awarding Agency.
Sort by Transaction Amount descending when screening for the largest obligation rows, but remember those are transaction amounts rather than award totals.
Capture generated_internal_id from the selected row even if it was not explicitly listed in fields, because source code appends it as a helper id.

workflows.name: Screen top transactions for one awarding agency
workflows.description: Use the live-backed agency-bounded template to isolate one awarding agency and inspect the returned transaction rows.

steps.action: Set filters.time_period, contract award_type_codes, and an agencies object with type=awarding, tier=toptier or subtier, and the desired agency name.

Request the compact screening columns Award ID, Mod, Recipient Name, Action Date, Transaction Amount, Awarding Agency, Awarding Sub Agency, and Award Type, then sort by Transaction Amount descending with a small limit.

caveats.statement: Response row shape is dynamic and driven by fields; do not assume every documented label appears in every row.
caveats.impact: Always inspect or control the requested fields set before downstream parsing or charting.

caveats.statement: Transaction search is transaction-grain, so repeated Award IDs across rows are normal.
caveats.impact: Row counts and sums answer transaction questions, not award-count questions.

caveats.statement: Transaction Amount is a row-level obligation measure rather than an award-total measure.
caveats.impact: Do not narrate top transaction rows as top awards without an award-level follow-up.

caveats.statement: Deep pagination is bounded by limit<=100 and a 50000-record result window.
caveats.impact: Use download workflows or other endpoints for very large exports.

caveats.statement: Program_activity appears in docs but may no longer be supported by the actual view validator.
caveats.impact: Prefer program_activities until live testing proves otherwise.

caveats.statement: The special award_type_codes value no intersection short-circuits to an empty 200 response and omits the normal messages array.
caveats.impact: Treat it as an upstream sentinel for an already-empty intersection, not as evidence that the endpoint found zero rows after a full normal search path.
